title: Antibody Complementarity Determining Regions (CDRs) design using Constrained Energy Model

problem.claim: Design antibody CDR loops while preserving their specific geometric shape.

gap.claim: Existing in silico methods face challenges in maintaining the specific geometry of CDR loops.

contributions.claim: Proposes a Constrained Energy Model for antibody CDR loop design.
Defines a constrained manifold to characterize CDR loop geometry constraints and learns an energy landscape on that manifold.
Theoretical analysis indicates that learning on the constrained manifold needs fewer samples than learning without that constraint.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The generated CDR loop geometry is automatically preserved.
Theoretical analysis reports lower sample complexity for constrained-manifold learning than for the unconstrained method.
Empirical studies report up to 33.4% relative reduction in 3D geometry error and 8.4% relative reduction in amino acid sequence perplexity compared with the best baseline method.

narrative_sequence.summary: Therapeutic antibodies are an important and expanding drug class, and CDRs determine antibody-antigen binding.
In silico methods have explored antibody CDR loop design, but preserving specific loop geometry remains challenging.
The paper introduces CEM, using a constrained manifold for CDR geometry and an energy model defined on that manifold.
The constrained approach is described as preserving generated loop geometry and requiring less sample complexity theoretically.
Empirical studies report improvements in geometry error and sequence perplexity over the best baseline, and the code is publicly available.

source_observation.claim: Representing domain-specific geometric constraints through a constrained manifold is reported to preserve generated CDR loop geometry.

interpretation.claim: Encoding structural constraints directly into the representation may reduce violations of important domain geometry during generation.

application.claim: For constrained scientific design tasks, consider modeling the feasible geometry explicitly before learning a generation or energy function.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond antibody CDR loop geometry or under which constraint regimes it is effective.

source_observation.claim: The authors report lower sample complexity theoretically and improvements in geometry error and sequence perplexity empirically.

interpretation.claim: Combining constraint-aware modeling with task-specific evaluation can improve both data efficiency and reported design metrics.

application.claim: Evaluate constrained models using both structural validity metrics and task-level quality metrics, alongside sample-efficiency analysis.

exception.claim: The abstract does not provide datasets, experimental protocols, uncertainty estimates, or details sufficient to assess independent reproducibility of the reported improvements.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the datasets or data splits.
The abstract does not specify the baseline methods or experimental protocol.
The abstract does not report uncertainty estimates or statistical testing details.
The abstract does not detail the constraint construction or optimization procedure.
